audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2 and 3 were credited to Vladimir in both layers while whys[1] says level 2 stays neutral and whys[2] calls level 3 a skill fight.
audit.why: Packet levelChart: Skill for rows 0-4, Vladimir for rows 5 and 6 — the scaling story the rest of the page already tells.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 and 2 to Skill as matched full/content pairs; ratings already read 5/10 and stay.

audit.why: The long even 1-5 stretch, the level 6 execution check, the first-item takeover and the two-item drain-tank window are all placed correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated ability names: his R is called 'Final Retribution' in three places and his E 'Golden Onslaught'. The real names are Grim Deliverance and Aureate Rush. His R is also described as 'lockdown' when Riot's text says it damages and heals him, and late calls his W a 'drain' when W is a stab-and-pull with no healing.
audit.why: Kit file: Q 10-6s, slashes twice, heals, auto reset, recast knocks up; W 850 range / 14-12s, damages then pulls toward him; E 10-8s dash with percent-health damage; R 600 range / 110/95/80s, heals for a portion of damage dealt. Names come from the missing-interactions records (The Darkin Glaive, Aureate Rush, Grim Deliverance).
audit.corrected: Real names in all four places, R described as a heal rather than lockdown, W's pull and 850 range and the Q reset tell written into the do's and don'ts with cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization carried no anti-heal line and nothing warned that stacking resistances misreads his E.
audit.why: His Q and R both heal him, and Aureate Rush deals percent-health damage.
audit.corrected: The anti-heal timing is now in spikes[1].text and the percent-health warning in dontsFull[1].d. I did not add an item to report[8].t — that is a build claim I cannot verify from the kits.

edits.before: His big cooldown. Poke around it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His R is 110s at rank 1 and heals him — commit only once it is spent.

edits.after: His Q slashes twice and resets his attack, then recasts to knock you up — step back on the wind-up.

edits.before: Zaahen wastes Ultimate — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Transfusion reaches 600 — poke, then leave before his E lands.

edits.before: That is Zaahen's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: His W stabs at 850 and pulls you in — never stand in a straight line to him.

edits.before: A long even stretch: your Transfusion sustain and E zoning offset his Q Darkin Glaive poke, and neither of you can force a kill without the other misplaying.

edits.before: Hemoplague amp versus his R Final Retribution lockdown is pure execution - Pool his R window and your ult swings any fight that follows.
edits.after: Hemoplague amp versus his R Grim Deliverance is pure execution - it heals him off the damage, so land anti-heal before your ult swings the fight.

edits.before: Level 6 changes the stakes but not the balance: Hemoplague turns any extended fight your way, while his R Final Retribution lockdown punishes a mistimed Pool - whoever lands their ultimate on their own terms wins the all-in, so play it patient and make him flash the first move.
edits.after: Level 6 changes the stakes but not the balance: Hemoplague turns any extended fight your way, while his R Grim Deliverance heals him back through a mistimed Pool - whoever lands their ultimate on their own terms wins the all-in, so play it patient and make him move first.

edits.before: Your first AP item is where the lane tips for good - Q and E become genuine burst and Pool invalidates the all-in window he spent all lane building toward. By two items you are a scaling drain-tank he cannot solve: his W drain and R sustain lose the healing race, and Hemoplague ends every teamfight he enters.
